newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ahmsa places $425 million Yankee bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ahmsa places $425 million Yankee bonds.

text.p: Mexican steel company Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) said on Tuesday it had placed Yankee bonds worth $425 million.

"Ahmsa last week successfully placed in a private placement two series of an international bond (Yankee bond) for $425 million, in a transaction which has now put almost all of the debt of the company in medium and long terms," the company said in a statement.
The sale was led by Merrill Lynch & Co and Santander Investment.
The $200 million of Series A bonds have a maturity of five years. The $225 million of Series B bonds are at a seven-year term.
The bond placement is part of a company strategy to refinance its debt at lower rates and longer maturities. Ahmsa's debt was around $1.5 billion at the end of 1996.
The company said the Yankee bonds would not increase its debt, as the issue will be used to pay off short-term obligations at higher interest rates.
